theory.title: comparatives, superlatives, too and enough
theory.explanation: Use comparative adjectives to compare two people or things and superlatives for the highest degree in a group. Too means more than is suitable; enough means as much as is needed. Use as…as for equality.
theory.tip: Identifica la relación entre las ideas y la intención del hablante antes de escoger la estructura.

content.passage: When Aisha joined an international student group, she discovered that greetings were different in every country. In some places, people shook hands; elsewhere, a smile was enough. She found that asking questions was more useful than making assumptions. At first, she felt too shy to join conversations, but the group was friendlier than she expected. The most helpful members explained local customs without judging anyone. Aisha realised that being open-minded was more important than knowing every rule.

content.audioTranscript: A: Our local group is organising an event for new neighbours. B: What activities are planned? A: We asked people what they needed and offered help. B: Some people had different ideas, but everyone listened carefully. A: We will not share private details without permission. B: And if the weather is bad? A: We will use the hall. Since the first meeting, we have been sharing updates.
